gilmoreosaurus:enwiki:4.title: Gilmoreosaurus (Reclassification as Gilmoreosaurus and subsequent research)

facts.statement: The genus Gilmoreosaurus was formally described by Brett-Surman in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Brett-Surman, 1979

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus is a genus of hadrosauromorphan dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus (meaning "Charles Whitney Gilmore's lizard") is a genus of hadrosauromorphan dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Asia.

facts.statement: The type species Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis lived 96 million years ago in the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: The type species is Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis, known from the Iren Dabasu Formation of Inner Mongolia, dating to 96 million years ago.

facts.statement: Initial excavations of Gilmoreosaurus fossils occurred over three days in April and May 1922.
facts.quote: The initial excavations of dinosaur fossils at Iren Dabasu took place on three days in April and May 1922.

facts.statement: George Olsen discovered Gilmoreosaurus fossils in quarries 145 and 149, located about 14 km northeast of Erenhot, approximately 1 km apart.
facts.quote: The material that would eventually come to be known as Gilmoreosaurus was discovered by George Olsen (a member of Granger's team) in two different quarries (145 and 149, about 1 km apart), around 14 km northeast of the town of Erenhot and not far from the border with Mongolia.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore published his description of Gilmoreosaurus in 1933.
facts.quote: He published his findings in 1933, describing both hadrosaurs as well as several other dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Species G. atavus and G. arkhangelskyi are classified as dubious due to being based on very fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: Additional specimens have been described as distinct species, including G. atavus from the Khodzhakul Formation of Uzbekistan, and G. arkhangelskyi from the Bissekty Formation, also of Uzbekistan. However, these are based on very fragmentary remains, and their classification is dubious.

facts.statement: Anatoly K. Rozhdestvensky debated in the 1960s that Bactrosaurus was a hadrosaurine rather than a lambeosaurine.
facts.quote: Anatoly K. Rozhdestvensky, in the 1960s, considered a different solution; that Bactrosaurus was in fact a hadrosaurine, not a lambeosaurine.

facts.statement: Future authors disagreed with Rozhdestvensky, reaffirming that Bactrosaurus is a lambeosaur and distinct from Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: Future authors would disagree, reaffirming the two hadrosaurs as distinct and Bactrosaurus as a lambeosaur.

facts.statement: Although fossils from several individuals were found, the material was disarticulated, making it impossible to determine which bones belonged to which individual.
facts.quote: Several individuals were represented and between them most of the skeleton found, but the material was disarticulated and so what pieces belonged to each individual is not possible to determine for certain.

facts.statement: Brett-Surman concluded that hadrosaurs originated in Asia based on Gilmoreosaurus, Bactrosaurus, and Probactrosaurus.
facts.quote: It was based in part on the two species, as well as on Probactrosaurus, that he concluded that hadrosaurs had originated in Asia.

facts.statement: Halszka Osmólska and Teresa Maryańska published comments on Asian hadrosaurs in 1981.
facts.quote: Halszka Osmólska and Teresa Maryańska published a paper in 1981 which focused on Saurolophus angustirostris, but also provided comments on Asian hadrosaurs as a whole.

facts.statement: John Horner and David B. Weishampel re-examined Iren Dabasu genera and undescribed material in 1985.
facts.quote: This would come to be in 1985, when Horner and David B. Weishampel would re-examine the material of both Iren Dabasu genera as well as material Gilmore never described, as had been indicated by Brett-Surman.

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues resolved the taxonomic issue in 1998 by describing new Bactrosaurus material.
facts.quote: The issue would finally be put to rest by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 1998, when they published a study describing newly discovered Bactrosaurus material.

facts.statement: Godefroit and colleagues suggested Bactrosaurus was a primitive hadrosauroid that was merely convergent with later relatives, explaining its paradoxical anatomy.
facts.quote: The reasoning for the paradoxical nature of the anatomy was that Bactrosaurus was not a lambeosaur or even hadrosaurid at all but instead a more primitive form of hadrosauroid merely convergent with its later relatives.

facts.statement: Albert Prieto-Márquez and Mark A. Norrel published a thorough redescription of Gilmoreosaurus in 2010.
facts.quote: Albert Prieto-Márquez and Mark A. Norrel began work on a thorough redescription of Gilmoreosaurus; this was published in 2010.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus was a large hadrosauroid that could grow up to 6.2 meters long and weigh between 1.2 and 3.6 tons.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus was a relatively large-sized hadrosauroid which could grow up to 6.2 m long and obtain weights between 1.2 to 3.6 t.

facts.statement: The right maxilla of Gilmoreosaurus preserves 26 alveolar foramina and 22 teeth-filled alveoli, though the total tooth count is likely unknown due to incomplete fossils.
facts.quote: On the inner side 26 alveolar foramen are preserved and 22 alveoli are filled with teeth but the total count may be unknown due to incompleteness

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus teeth were oval-shaped with a pinched upper end and coarse denticles featuring three small pointed structures.
facts.quote: The teeth are oval-shaped with a moderately pinched upper end and have coarse denticles, these denticles have three diminutive pointed structures.

facts.statement: The total number of teeth in the lower jaw of Gilmoreosaurus was likely fewer than 30.
facts.quote: The total dentary teeth count on Gilmoreosaurus was probably less than 30

facts.statement: A complete predentary bone from Gilmoreosaurus is U-shaped and bears numerous pointed denticles on its dorsal surface.
facts.quote: The predentary is represented by a complete element of specimen AMNH FARB 6369, which has a U-shaped form.

facts.statement: Fossil specimens of Gilmoreosaurus include four cervical, ten dorsal, seven sacral, and thirty-three caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column is represented by four cervical, ten dorsal, seven sacral and thirty three caudal vertebrae of several specimens.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Gilmoreosaurus have opisthocoelous centra that are heart-shaped from behind and flattened on the inner side.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae of specimens AMNH FARB 30671-30673 have centra that are opisthocoelous (concave on their posterior sides), heart-shaped in a posterior view and flattened on the inner side.

facts.statement: The neural spines on the dorsal vertebrae of Gilmoreosaurus are very elongated, subrectangular, and slightly curved toward the rear.
facts.quote: The neural spines are very elongated and subrectangular in shape, they are slightly curved to the posterior side.

facts.statement: The bottom surface of the fused sacral vertebrae in Gilmoreosaurus features a central ridge-like structure similar to that found in Bactrosaurus, Claosaurus, or Iguanodon.
facts.quote: When seen from the bottom surface, a ridge-like structure is located at the center as in Bactrosaurus, Claosaurus or Iguanodon.

facts.statement: The caudal vertebrae of Gilmoreosaurus have very flattened centra with small neural canals and neural spines projecting toward the rear.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae have very flattened centra with smally neural canals and neural spines that are projected towards the rear

facts.statement: The coracoid bone has an oval shape with a prominent foramen for the supracoracoid nerve, and the glenoid is D-shaped.
facts.quote: The coracoid has an oval-shaped form with a prominent coracoid foramen through which the supracoracoid nerve passes and the glenoid is D-shaped.

facts.statement: The bottom articulation of the coracoid is shortened, triangular, and directed downward, differing from the lateral hook seen in many other hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: The bottom articulation is shortened and triangular, as well as directed to the bottom area rather than hooked from the rear to the bottom in a lateral as in many other hadrosauroids and not hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: The scapula is very straight when viewed from above, with an inner surface that is flattened for most of its length.
facts.quote: The scapula is very straight in a top view with its inner surface being flattened throughout most of the length.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest extends from the upper half of the humerus to the lower side, with a bottom extension width-to-shaft diameter ratio of 1.67.
facts.quote: The deltopectoral crest—where the deltoid muscle was attached to the upper front of the humerus—is developed to the lower side from the upper half of the humerus, and its bottom extension has a total width diameter of the humeral shaft ratio of 1.67.

facts.statement: A large tuberosity is located on the posterior surface of the humerus, approximately one-third of the distance from the upper end.
facts.quote: A large tuberosity can be observed on the posterior surface of the humerus—about 1/3 the distance from the upper end.

facts.statement: The ilium is elongated and shallow, with a preacetabular process that is long and deflected toward the bottom.
facts.quote: The ilium is elongated and shallow in shape with its preacetabular process (anterior expansion of the iliac blade) also being long and deflected towards the bottom.

facts.statement: The supraacetabular process has an asymmetrical, V-shaped profile with a lateral projection tilted toward the bottom.
facts.quote: The supraacetabular process (a bony projection at the top border of the ilium) has an asymmetrical, v-shaped appearance in profile and its lateral projection is tilted to the bottom.

facts.statement: The ischium is notoriously elongated and features a wide, robust iliac peduncle that connects to the ilium.
facts.quote: The ischium is notoriously elongated and has a wide and robust iliac peduncle—tubercle-like structure that connects to the ilium.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had a femur similar to other hadrosauroids, featuring a well-developed fourth trochanter and lateral-inner condyles.
facts.quote: This element is mostly similar in build to other hadrosauroids with a well-developed fourth trochanter and lateral-inner condyles.

facts.statement: Approximately six tibia fossils were found in the Gilmoreosaurus collection.
facts.quote: One of the most common elements among the collection is represented by the tibia—about six elements.

facts.statement: The Gilmoreosaurus tibia was a robust bone slightly shorter than the femur with a cylindrical shaft expanded at both ends, more so at the lower end.
facts.quote: It is a robust element that is slightly shorter than the femur, and is composed of a rather cylindrical shaft that is expanded at both upper and lower ends; more expanded at the latter though.

facts.statement: The Gilmoreosaurus tibia featured a very elongated and developed cnemial crest near its upper end.
facts.quote: The cnemial crest is very elongated and developed near the upper end of the bone.

facts.statement: Adult Gilmoreosaurus tibiae showed a more developed bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus compared to juveniles.
facts.quote: A main difference between the juvenile and adult tibiae can be noted by the bottom tilt of the lateral malleolus—this trait is less developed in juveniles.

facts.statement: The Gilmoreosaurus fibula was particularly straight and elongated.
facts.quote: The fibula is particularly straight and elongated.

facts.statement: The astragalus was the largest tarsal element in the Gilmoreosaurus foot.
facts.quote: Among the tarsal elements, the astragalus is the largest.

facts.statement: The Gilmoreosaurus foot contained metatarsals III and IV.
facts.quote: Among the metatarsus elements, metatarsal III and IV are present.

facts.statement: The pedal unguals of Gilmoreosaurus were more arrow-shaped and sharply developed than those of other hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: These elements are more arrow-shaped and more sharply developed than in hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: Analysis of bone microstructure suggests Gilmoreosaurus shared similar growth size and rates with other large hadrosauroids like Gobihadros.
facts.quote: This analysis suggests similar growth size and rates in these species.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus exhibited a decrease in secondary remodelling in the tibia, an adaptation allowing the bone to bear higher tensions associated with increasing body size.
facts.quote: The first important adaptation was the decrease of secondary remodelling in the tibia, allowing the bone to bear higher tensions.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus showed a disappearance of lines of arrested growth (LAGs), a feature allowing uninterrupted growth during its life, similar to giant sauropods.
facts.quote: A second adaptation was the disappearance of lines of arrested growth (LAGs). This feature, also reported in giant sauropods, allowed uninterrupted growth during ontogeny.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tumors found on Gilmoreosaurus caudal vertebrae may have been caused by environmental factors or genetic inheritance.
facts.quote: The tumors were only found on caudal vertebrae and they may have been caused by environmental factors, such as the way in which these hadrosaurs interacted with their environments, making them more susceptible to get cancer, or, through genetic inheritance.

facts.statement: In 2007, Rothschild and Tanke reported that osteochondrosis was particularly common in rapidly growing hadrosaurs like Gilmoreosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2007, Rothschild and Tanke reported the increased presence of osteochondrosis in hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 95.8 ± 6.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus is known from the Late Cretaceous Iren Dabasu Formation, which has been dated back to the Cenomanian stage around 95.8 ± 6.2 million years ago.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus likely acted as a medium to low-level browser in its ecosystem.
facts.quote: Ponderous herbivorous animals like Gilmoreosaurus and Bactrosaurus may have been medium to low-level browsers.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus likely preyed upon by the fast-running tyrannosauroid Alectrosaurus, as their geographic ranges overlapped.
facts.quote: The geographic range of Gilmoreosaurus overlapped with the fast-running tyrannosauroid Alectrosaurus, likely being the prey item for this theropod.

facts.statement: It is debated whether osteochondrosis was truly absent in Gilmoreosaurus, as the low sample size might have led to false negatives despite the disease being common in other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Though they examined several other dinosaur groups, this disease appears to be particularly common in hadrosaurs, which were rapidly growing animals.

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus is a genus represented by four species of hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus ("lagarto de Gilmore") es un género representado por 4 especies de dinosaurios ornitópodos hadrosauroides

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus lived from the middle to late Cretaceous, approximately 120 to 70 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: vivieron de mediados a finales del período Cretácico desde el Aptiense al Campaniense, hace aproximadamente entre 120 a 70 millones de años en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had large lower jaws and long hind legs but lacked a hollow crest.
facts.quote: tenían grandes las mandíbulas inferiores y las patas traseras largas y no tenían la cresta hueca

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus feet resembled those of iguanodontians like Iguanodon rather than later hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: Sus pies con aspecto de garra se parecían más a las de un iguanodóntido, como el Iguanodon, que a las de un hadrosáurido

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had a light build for its size of around seven meters in length.
facts.quote: Era de constitución ligera para su tamaño de alrededor de siete metros de largo

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had well-developed hind limbs that would have allowed it to run quickly.
facts.quote: con miembros posteriores bien desarrollados que le permitirían una rápida carrera

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus had a mouth full of small teeth that replaced themselves as they wore down, similar to later hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: Su boca está repleta de pequeños dientes que se remplazaban a medida que se desgastaban, como en hadrosáuridos posteriores

facts.statement: The first fossil remains of Gilmoreosaurus were collected by George Olsen in 1923.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos fósiles de Gilmoreosaurus fueron recolectados por George Olsen en 1923

facts.statement: The type species was originally described as Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis in 1923 and renamed Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis in 1979.
facts.quote: La especie tipo fue descripta como Mandschurosaurus mongoliensis en 1923 fue renombrada en 1979 con el nombre actual Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis

facts.statement: The type species Gilmoreosaurus mongoliensis was found in Mongolia from the Iren Dabasu Formation, dating to 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: restos encontrados en Mongolia, de la formación Iren Dabasu, que data de 70 millones de años

facts.statement: A new species, Gilmoreosaurus atavus, was described in 1995 by Nessov from the Khodzhakul Formation in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Una nueva especie Gilmoreosaurus atavus se conoció en 1995 por Nessov de la formación Khodzhakul de Uzbekistán

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus arkhangelskyi was found in the Bissekty Formation, dating to 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: Gilmoreosaurus arkhangelskyi de la formación Bissekty, hace 89 millones de años

facts.statement: Gilmoreosaurus kysylkumensis, also from the Bissekty Formation, is sometimes included but has also been referred to the related genus Bactrosaurus.
facts.quote: Una especie adicional , Gilmoreosaurus kysylkumensis, también de la formación Bissekty, se incluye a veces, aunque también se ha referido al género relacionado Bactrosaurus

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Prieto-Márquez and Norell placed Gilmoreosaurus in a sister group closely related to Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: un estudio de 2010 realizado por Prieto-Márquez y Norell coloca al animal en un grupo externo estrechamente relacionado con Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: In 2003, evidence of tumors including hemangiomas, desmoplastic fibroma, metastatic cancer, and osteoma was found in fossilized Gilmoreosaurus skeletons.
facts.quote: En 2003, se descubrió evidencia de tumores, incluidos hemangiomas, fibroma desmoplásico, cáncer metastásico y osteoma en esqueletos de Gilmoreosaurus fosilizados

facts.statement: Although more than 10,000 fossils were examined this way, tumors were limited to Gilmoreosaurus and closely related genera.
facts.quote: Aunque se examinaron más de 10000 fósiles de esta manera, los tumores se limitaron a Gilmoreosaurus y géneros estrechamente relacionados

facts.statement: It is debated whether species like G. atavus and G. arkhangelskyi are valid, as they are based on very fragmentary remains and their classification is doubtful.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estos se basan en restos muy fragmentarios, y su clasificación es dudosa

facts.statement: Many consider Gilmoreosaurus to be one of the most primitive hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: Es considerado por muchos como uno de los hadrosáuridos más primitivos
